images.name: cover
images.title: Which job should your *first AI Employee* do?
images.sub: Start with the dullest job in the building. Five tests to run on any role, and the jobs that usually pass.

images.name: five-tests
images.title: Five tests for a *first job*
head: Test
Ask
Passes
Fails
rows: Does the same request arrive many times a week?
Could you explain it in a few pages?
Can an error be fixed the same day?
A wire to the wrong account
Is it all email, phone and systems?
Will one person read its log daily?
images.source: A role that fails any test is a job for later

images.name: first-jobs
images.title: Jobs that usually *pass first*
rows: Books, changes and cancels appointments, answers hours and directions, hands unusual calls to a person
Answers order status and return questions from written policy, escalates complaints
Books viewings, repairs and appointments, sends reminders, fills cancellations
Moves invoices and intake forms into your systems, checks each before saving
Chases unsigned letters, missing documents and overdue invoices on a schedule
Prepares the case and the numbers, then waits for a person to approve

images.name: quote
images.text: Give your first AI Employee *the dullest job in the building.* The one with the most volume and mistakes you can undo the same afternoon.

images.name: pick-the-job
images.title: How to *pick the first job*
steps: Take two or three roles and write down every task that comes back week after week.
Ask the person doing the work how long each task takes in a normal week.
Cross out any task that fails one. What's left is the shortlist.
Choose the tasks with the most hours and the fewest exceptions. That's the first job.
One paragraph, the person it reports to, and what it can do alone versus what it asks about.
